report.summary: Reviewed the fixed-scope noodle packet (delivery-assessment, source findings, label citations, literal directive, evidence scope, contracts, evidence export, scope clarifications, two tests) for concrete P1/P2 defects. The row-context rewrite is absent, and raw modelJudgment keeps the untrimmed decoded explanation, status and resolved citations. The Chinese quoted-label grammar correctly rejects unquoted operational or second-frame prefixes, and treats quoted action-like labels as data. Evidence export recomputes sourceFinding from files plus the historical scope prefix, and a conflicting F2 file is rejected by the domain. I found no new concrete P1/P2 defect that can be shown with an exact, source-supported repro under these constraints.
limitations: Read-only source review. No files were changed and no typecheck, build, tests, browser, provider or API checks were run.

Review is limited to the supplied packet files. Callers and helpers outside the packet (business-checks, source-business-evidence, static-project, publication policy, assessment-completion, runtime-project, proof-demo) are taken as given and not verified.
The parser (parse5) and normalization helpers are not in the packet, so parse5 DOM/source-offset behavior was reasoned about from its documented API rather than observed.

Scope is deliberately narrow (the fixed noodle scope). Generic defects outside the changed boundaries, such as the leading-whitespace handling of the top-level completion text() call in delivery-assessment (line 253), were not treated as regression findings here.
No inferred regex claims about repeated-frame Chinese repro strings were made, per instruction.

sourceFinding is assessed only as source facts from the exact exported files plus the historical scope prefix. Rendering, visibility, persistence, provider execution, authentication and payment are not attested.
